quotations.old_english: Seó rédelse, and ðæt geþeaht úrra feónda geleorde [MS. geleorode], ðá hí hit endian sceoldon
Ðonne heora hwylc of weorulde geleored wæs
quotations.latin: cum quis eōrum de sæcŭlo fuisset evŏcātus

source_text: ge-leoran; p. de; pp. ed To go, depart, emigrate, die; &i-long;re, migr&a-long;re, emigr&a-long;re, def&i-short;c&e-short;re :-- Mec geleoran lǽt let me depart, Exon. 118 b; Th. 455, 3; Hy. 4, 44 : Bd. 4, 23; S. 596, 11. Ic ná geleore non emigr&a-long;bo, Ps. Spl. C. 61, 6. Seó rédelse, and ðæt geþeaht úrra feónda geleorde [MS. geleorode], ðá hí hit endian sceoldon in&i-short;m&i-long;ci def&e-long;c&e-long;runt fr&a-short;meæ in f&i-long;nem, Ps. Th. 9, 6. Ðonne heora hwylc of weorulde geleored wæs cum quis e&o-long;rum de sæc&u-short;lo fuisset ev&o-short;c&a-long;tus, Bd. 4, 23; S. 595, 41, note. Sægde Hilde of weorulde geleoran nunciavit Hild migrasse de sæculo, 596, 11. Ne gelioraþ non præteribit, Mt. Kmbl. Lind. 24, 34. Dóhter mín geliored is filia mea defuncta est, 9, 18.
